extracted.intended_audience: readers and decision-makers concerned with early-modern maritime discovery proposals (monarchs, viceroys, pilots, navigators, historians)
extracted.subtask_description: Writing and submitting a voyage/discovery narrative and proposal for royal or official support, including navigational evidence, logistics, and persuasive argumentation for settling or exploring newly found islands and regions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior navigational experience in the relevant regions
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposer should be 'a great pilot with much experience of the South Sea and of the great gulf between the coasts of New Spain and Peru and Japan and the Philippine Islands' and have served in major navigational roles (e.g., Chief Pilot of a prior voyage).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support claims with prior positions and voyage history (such as having been Chief Pilot of Mendaña’s voyage); emphasize direct experience of the specific seas and coasts involved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters of introduction and high-level endorsements
rubrics_metrics.description: Supply letters from influential patrons and authorities (examples given: letters from the Viceroy of Peru, the Duke of Sesa, the Ambassador at Rome, and even the Pope/His Holiness).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain and present formal recommendations and introductions from high officials and clergy to strengthen the proposal and secure audience with the sovereign or council.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission of papers, charts and physical evidence for scrutiny
rubrics_metrics.description: Present 'papers and charts' and other documentary evidence (including invented instruments) to experts and officials so they can examine the proposal's basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bring detailed charts, globes, and any instruments or demonstrations that exhibit the proposer's technical competence; make these available to mathematicians, pilots, and geographers for inspection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expert verification through mathematicians and pilots
rubrics_metrics.description: Have the proposal and evidence examined by distinguished mathematicians and geographers (the text cites Fathers Clavio and Villalpando, Doctors Toribio Perez and Masa) who can judge the 'proofs and reasonings'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek institutional or learned endorsement: convene experts to review charts and instruments, and record their conclusions that the claims are 'probable' or 'worthy to be put into execution.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear memorial/plan specifying route, method and measurable objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a concrete plan such as travelling 'from Spain by the Strait of Magellan and return by the Eastern Indies, having gone round the world' and including scientific aims (e.g., measuring needle variation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detail the intended route, stages, ships to be used, scientific or navigational objectives, and how the voyage will be conducted so officials can assess feasibility and value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Argue the benefits to God and the Crown (motive & utility)
rubrics_metrics.description: Frame the enterprise as 'a business of great service to God and to the King' (examples: 'saving an infinity of souls', strategic advantage against rivals, economic and territorial gains).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain religious, strategic, economic, and imperial advantages of the discovery to persuade sovereign authorities; address counterarguments about cost and maintenance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrate personal fitness and moral character
rubrics_metrics.description: Show personal qualities: being 'a worker, quiet, disinterested, of decent life, zealous for the service of God and for my service' are cited as desirable traits for a leader of such an enterprise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide testimony or reputation evidence about the proposer's temperament, probity, piety, and industriousness to reassure patrons and the crown about reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Logistical preparedness: ships, crews, provisions and ports
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare concrete logistical details (the narrative lists four vessels, 'a list of four hundred persons', taking-in-water at ports like Paita, victualling, and provisioning the fleet).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include an inventory of vessels and crew, provisioning plans, intended stopping places for water and supplies, and contingency plans for sickness, shortages, and ship losses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detailed geographic and natural-resource reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Reports should document island sizes, latitudes, anchorage quality, natural resources (pigs, plantains, nuts, ginger, rivers, springs, marble, pearls), flora/fauna, volcanoes and navigational hazards, and native population descriptions and behaviors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record precise latitudes, distances, descriptions of ports, availability of fresh water and food, local products, and any features important for settlement or navigation; include notes on natives' disposition and arms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise operational secrecy until sovereign informed
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain confidentiality of discoveries: 'it is fit that the first islands should remain concealed until His Majesty be informed... the English, on knowing it, might settle in them'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommend withholding precise locations and sensitive intelligence until official instructions are received from the sovereign to prevent rival powers from exploiting the discovery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide demonstrable technical competence in navigation and instruments
rubrics_metrics.description: Exhibit mastery of navigational art: 'expert in making globes, and charts for navigating; that he well understands the use of instruments necessary for navigation, and that he showed them two of his own invention...'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detail instrument designs, methods for taking altitudes and accounting for magnetic variation, and offer to measure and clarify ambiguous navigational phenomena (e.g., needle variation) as part of the voyage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address feasibility and cost objections with reasoned arguments
rubrics_metrics.description: Respond to sceptics who say 'sufficient lands had been discovered... what signified was to people and settle them, rather than go in search of those I said were new' by submitting 'new memorials... representing the arguments in favour of the enterprise'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anticipate objections about cost, distance, and maintenance; prepare reasoned counter-arguments and additional evidence to justify undertaking costly, long-range expeditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record and report on encounters and conduct during settlement attempts
rubrics_metrics.description: Document interactions with natives, incidents of theft or violence, internal discipline and misconduct among crew (e.g., executions, improvised governance), and health crises affecting the expedition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include candid accounts of difficulties encountered during attempted settlement (disease, leadership deaths, morale, violence) so future expeditions and authorities can learn and plan safeguards.
